comments.body:
## WHERE the state lives, and WHO can read it — the containment question, answered

Requested follow-up. All read-only; only digests and lengths were ever computed, never a value.

### Location: REMOTE, in S3, encrypted at rest with SSE-S3 (not a CMK)

`infra/terraform/versions.tf:13-19`:

    backend "s3" {
      bucket       = "rebar-tfstate-896586841071"
      key          = "rebar/prod/terraform.tfstate"
      region       = "us-east-1"
      encrypt      = true
      use_lockfile = true
    }

Bucket posture, from the live API:

    default encryption      SSE-S3 / AES256   (BucketKeyEnabled=false; SSE-C blocked)
    public access block     BlockPublicAcls=true  IgnorePublicAcls=true
                            BlockPublicPolicy=true  RestrictPublicBuckets=true
    bucket policy           NONE (GetBucketPolicy -> NoSuchBucketPolicy)
    bucket ACL              a single FULL_CONTROL grant to the account canonical owner
    versioning              ENABLED

There is no local `terraform.tfstate` in the repo — the state is remote-only, so this is not a
laptop-file exposure.

Two things follow from the encryption line. It is **SSE-S3 (AES256), not a KMS CMK**, so there is
no separate key policy and no per-decrypt CloudTrail data event to constrain or observe access —
`s3:GetObject` alone is sufficient, and encryption-at-rest adds nothing against a principal who
already has that permission. And because there is **no bucket policy at all**, access is governed
**solely by IAM identity policies** in account `896586841071`; there is no resource-side allow-list
to narrow it.

### Who can read it: contained to account-admin principals

Resolved with `iam simulate-principal-policy` against the exact state object ARN rather than by
reading policy documents, so this is the effective decision, not an inferred one:

    arn:aws:iam::896586841071:role/rebar-gerrit-instance-role   s3:GetObject -> implicitDeny
    arn:aws:iam::896586841071:user/joe_frontier                 s3:GetObject -> allowed

**The good news, and it is the load-bearing fact: the EC2 instance role CANNOT read the state.**
`rebar-gerrit-instance-role` carries only `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore` plus three narrow inline
policies (`rebar-gerrit-bedrock-converse`, `rebar-gerrit-cloudwatch-basic`,
`rebar-gerrit-ssm-params-read`). So compromising the internet-facing box — the containers, Gerrit,
the MCP server — does **not** hand over the state file and its 23 cleartext secrets. The box can
read the SSM parameters it is scoped to, which is the intended, far narrower grant.

The account holds exactly **one IAM user, `joe_frontier`** (an administrator, and the identity
these read-only checks ran under), plus `OrganizationAccountAccessRole` for cross-account org
admin. Every other role is an unrelated `lmn-*` application role.

**Verdict on containment: CONTAINED, not exposed.** The reachable set is account administrators,
who can already read the underlying SSM SecureStrings directly. This is not a privilege-escalation
path from the box, and it is not public. That materially lowers the urgency relative to the
original filing.

### The part that is NOT contained: 149 retained versions

    aws s3api list-object-versions --prefix rebar/prod/terraform.tfstate -> 149 versions

Versioning is enabled and there is no lifecycle expiry on noncurrent versions, so **every secret
value that has ever passed through this state remains readable in an older object version**. The
consequence is the one worth acting on: **rotating a secret does not remove it from the state
history.** A key rotated after a suspected exposure is still sitting in cleartext in a prior
version, and `s3api get-object --version-id` retrieves it. Any remediation that only fixes the
current state leaves the historical tail in place, so the tail needs its own decision — noncurrent
version expiry, or an explicit accept.

### Net reassessment

Contained to admins, so not an emergency — but the 149-version tail means the exposure window is
unbounded in time rather than a point-in-time snapshot, and SSE-S3 gives no key-policy or
data-event control over reads. Priority raised P2 -> P1 accordingly.

No remediation attempted, per instruction.

comments.body: ORCHESTRATOR TRIAGE (2026-08-29): Held for an operator SECURITY-DESIGN decision before any fix is dispatched. The mechanism (SSM SecureString values persisted in cleartext in terraform state, collapsing the secret tier to the state-bucket ACL) is a genuine defect, but the remediation is a design choice, not a mechanical fix — options include moving secrets out of terraform-managed state (create-ignore_changes + out-of-band seeding), a dedicated secrets manager, or hardening state-at-rest/ACL posture. Each changes the deployment/secret-handling contract. Awaiting operator direction on the target posture; will dispatch a /rebar-debug repair once the design target is set.

## Plan-review round 1 (BLOCK) — findings addressed (narration moved here to fit the 8000-char plan cap)

Round-1 LLM plan-review (bedrock sonnet) returned BLOCK with three blocking findings; all are addressed in the revised plan. Detail kept here so the description stays within the review admission cap:

**1 & 2 — G1G2, unenumerated consumers of the old `ignore_changes` contract.** Two GATING consumers assert the opcert key still declares `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }` and would regress to RED:
- `infra/terraform/opcert-plan-assertions.sh` assertion **(f)** hard-fails (exit 1) unless `opcert.tf` declares that block on `opcert_ed25519_key`. Fix: rewrite (f) to assert the key param declares `value_wo` (+ `value_wo_version`) — the new no-clobber invariant.
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py` — `test_terraform_both_securestring_params_present` (line 69, key-param `ignore_changes` regex) and `test_assertion_script_present_executable_and_literal` (line 164, asserts the script contains `.lifecycle_meta_arguments.ignore_changes`). Both move to the `value_wo` invariant; the `opcert_origin_guard` guard-param assertions are unchanged.
- Non-gating but directly-related docs refreshed: `infra/runbooks/sso-auth-host.md` (cookie-signing row) and `infra/runbooks/gerrit-auth-hardening.md`.
- Verified there are NO other test/script consumers asserting value/ignore on `rebar_secrets` or `cookie_signing_secret` (`grep` across `tests/`, `scripts/`, `infra/`). `test_mcp_on_box_infra.py:553` asserts on `rebar_plain_seeded` (a non-secret String param) — out of scope.

**3 — G6, the CUTOVER clobber.** Correct and important: on the migration apply, `value_wo_version` transitions ABSENT→1, which the AWS provider treats as a change and re-sends `value_wo = "CHANGEME"`, RESETTING each already-seeded live secret to the placeholder on that single apply. Steady-state no-clobber still holds (value re-sent only on a later `value_wo_version` bump). Reconciliation: this reset is acceptable and INTENDED because the same exposure mandates ROTATING these secrets anyway — the deferred operator ticket runs the apply and the re-seed/rotation in ONE maintenance window (apply → all affected slots are `CHANGEME` → operator seeds the NEW rotated value into each via `aws ssm put-parameter --overwrite`), with `user_data.sh`'s `CHANGEME` fail-fast as the safety net and a back-out note in the runbook. The code change runs no apply.

**RED→GREEN oracle result (prototyped hermetically against copies of the three .tf files):** the guard is RED on the current tree with exactly 6 findings (the 3 seeded-secret resources × {literal-value, ignore_changes}); `opcert_origin_guard` (generated value) and the `String` params are correctly NOT flagged; GREEN (exit 0) after the value_wo migration; and reverting one param to `value + ignore_changes` returns it to RED (mutation teeth).

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Every operator-seeded SSM `SecureString` secret in `infra/terraform` persists its CLEARTEXT value in
the remote terraform state (S3 `rebar-tfstate-896586841071`, key `rebar/prod/terraform.tfstate`,
SSE-S3 not a CMK). The `value = "CHANGEME"` + `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }` pattern stops
terraform WRITING the secret from git, but terraform still READS the live value into
`attributes.value` on every refresh/import, so the plaintext lands in state — `terraform state pull`
renders 23 secrets in cleartext to any state-bucket reader, collapsing the secret tier to the bucket
ACL. Root cause is proven (see evidence comments).

## Decision (operator-approved — Option 1)

Migrate every operator-seeded `SecureString` SECRET from `value = "CHANGEME"` + `ignore_changes =
[value]` to terraform WRITE-ONLY arguments `value_wo` + `value_wo_version`, which the AWS provider
NEVER stores to state ("write-only values are never stored to state"). Non-secret `String` params
(`jira-url`, `jira-user`, `jira-project`) and the terraform-GENERATED `SecureString`
`opcert_origin_guard` (value = `random_password.opcert_guard.result`, already in state via the random
resource + API-Gateway header, so `value_wo` gives no net benefit) stay as-is.

## Approach

Three resources carry the antipattern and move to `value_wo` + `value_wo_version = 1` (dropping
`value` and the `ignore_changes` lifecycle block):
- `aws_ssm_parameter.rebar_secrets` (for_each, 18 params) — `infra/terraform/ssm.tf:90`
- `aws_ssm_parameter.opcert_ed25519_key` — `infra/terraform/opcert.tf:52`
- `aws_ssm_parameter.cookie_signing_secret` — `infra/terraform/auth_sso.tf:39`

`value_wo` needs AWS provider ≥ 5.79 and write-only args need terraform ≥ 1.11 (host: terraform
1.15.8, provider/lock 5.100.0). `versions.tf` floors sit below both today, so raise them:
`required_version >= 1.10` → `>= 1.11`; AWS `~> 5.0` → `~> 5.79`. Rationale: write-only args are the
provider-native mechanism purpose-built for keeping a secret out of state — no new dependency,
secrets-manager, or KMS CMK; minimal blast radius.

**Steady-state vs. cutover (G6, addressed):** in steady state the write-only value is re-sent only
when `value_wo_version` changes, so an out-of-band-seeded value is never reverted and `user_data.sh`'s
`CHANGEME` fail-fast still fires on an unseeded slot. The ONE migration apply is different: because
`value_wo_version` goes ABSENT→1, the provider re-sends `value_wo = "CHANGEME"` once and RESETS each
already-seeded live value to the placeholder. That is intended and safe here because the exposure
mandates ROTATING these secrets anyway — the deferred operator ticket does the apply + re-seed/rotate
in one window; the code change runs no apply. Detail in the round-1 comment + the new runbook.

**Unenumerated consumers (G1G2, addressed):** `infra/terraform/opcert-plan-assertions.sh` (f) and
`tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py` assert the opcert key's `ignore_changes = [value]`; both move
to the `value_wo` invariant in lockstep. Directly-related docs `infra/runbooks/sso-auth-host.md` and
`infra/runbooks/gerrit-auth-hardening.md` are refreshed off the stale `ignore_changes` wording.

## Scope (files)

- `infra/terraform/ssm.tf`, `opcert.tf`, `auth_sso.tf` — migrate the three secret resources.
- `infra/terraform/versions.tf` — raise terraform + AWS-provider floors.
- `infra/terraform/opcert-plan-assertions.sh` — assertion (f) → `value_wo` invariant.
- `scripts/check_ssm_secret_state.py` (NEW) — hermetic structural guard (no live AWS) over
  `infra/terraform/*.tf`: every `SecureString` `aws_ssm_parameter` is flagged for a quoted
  string-literal `value` and/or `ignore_changes = [value]`, must pair `value_wo` with
  `value_wo_version`, and the generated-value case (unquoted-expression `value`, no `ignore_changes`)
  is allowed. Modeled on `scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py`.
- `Makefile` — wire the guard into `make lint` (next to `check_templatefile_escapes.py`, line 302).
- `tests/unit/test_check_ssm_secret_state.py` (NEW) — RED→GREEN + mutation teeth + committed-tree
  clean + make-lint wiring, mirroring `tests/unit/test_check_templatefile_escapes.py`.
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py` — the two consumers → `value_wo` invariant.
- `docs/adr/0105-ssm-secrets-never-in-terraform-state.md` + `docs/adr/.numbers/0105` + regenerated
  `docs/adr/README.md` — record the decision, extending ADR 0008, relating to ADR 0046.
- `infra/runbooks/ssm-secret-write-only.md` (NEW) — declare/seed/rotate + remediation cutover.
- `infra/runbooks/sso-auth-host.md`, `infra/runbooks/gerrit-auth-hardening.md` — refresh stale wording.

## Testing

- RED first: guard/test fail on the CURRENT tree for the right reason (three secrets persist a
  `value` literal + `ignore_changes`), proven before the fix.
- GREEN after: guard + test pass once the three resources use `value_wo`/`value_wo_version`.
- Mutation teeth: reverting any one param to `value = "…" + ignore_changes = [value]` returns the
  guard to RED (asserted by the new test).
- `terraform validate` in `infra/terraform` passes (static; no plan/apply against the real backend).
- Updated `tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py` passes; `make lint` passes.
- No secret VALUE is printed, logged, or committed — the guard inspects HCL structure only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The three seeded-secret resources use `value_wo` + `value_wo_version` and carry no
      `value`/`ignore_changes = [value]`; verified by `scripts/check_ssm_secret_state.py` exit 0 + diff.
- [ ] The guard is RED pre-fix, GREEN post-fix, and RED again on a one-param revert; verified by
      `tests/unit/test_check_ssm_secret_state.py`.
- [ ] The guard is wired into `make lint`; verified by a wiring test and `make lint` exit 0.
- [ ] `versions.tf` floors are terraform `>= 1.11` and AWS `~> 5.79`; verified by reading the file.
- [ ] `terraform validate` in `infra/terraform` exits 0.
- [ ] `opcert-plan-assertions.sh` (f) + `tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py` assert the `value_wo`
      invariant and pass; verified by running the opcert test file.
- [ ] ADR 0105 + marker `docs/adr/.numbers/0105` exist, the index is regenerated, and
      `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py` + `python scripts/gen_adr_index.py --check` pass.
- [ ] `infra/runbooks/ssm-secret-write-only.md` covers declare/seed/rotate + the remediation cutover
      and cross-links ADR 0105; verified by reading it.
- [ ] A deferred OPERATOR `task` ticket (apply → re-seed/rotate in one window → verify no SecureString
      value in `terraform state pull` → rotate crown-jewels) exists, linked `discovered_from` this
      ticket; verified by `show_ticket`. [non-codebase] evidence: the new ticket id in a comment.
- [ ] No credential value is printed, logged, or committed by the fix or its verification.
